# Problem Statement
You are an optimization modeling agent working on a real-world oriented
three-dimensional bin packing benchmark. Your task is to inspect the local
files, understand the loading instructions, and submit a feasible packing plan

## Background

There are two identical bins of size 900 x 900 x 900. The 38 physical cases are
expanded in `data/cases.csv` from the 10 item categories in `data/items.csv`.
Each case may be rotated into any of the six axis-aligned orientations.

The packing must be physically feasible: each case must be inside exactly one
bin and cases in the same bin must not overlap. Each bin has a maximum total
weight of 800. Additional rules from the paper require certain item categories
to be colocated, certain categories to be separated, and non-heavy categories to
be above heavy categories when they share a bin.

The warehouse team also added practical loading rules: upper cases need enough
support underneath, fragile or weak cargo must not be crushed, and the driver
must be able to unload earlier stops before later stops without digging through
the load.

## Business Goal

Pack all cases into the available bins while satisfying physical and
operational restrictions. Among feasible packings, prefer fewer used bins,
lower packed height, and better load balance around the target center of mass.

The checker gives the best score to packings that use fewer bins first. When
two packings use the same number of bins, it prefers lower stacks and better
weight balance around the published center-of-mass target. The center-of-mass
target is used for scoring and comparison, not as an absolute pass/fail rule,
because the source article gives a target point but not a tolerance.

## Packing Rules

1. Every case in `data/cases.csv` must be assigned to exactly one bin listed in
   `data/bins.csv`.

2. Coordinates are local to the assigned bin. A submitted case must start
   inside the bin, use nonnegative coordinates and sizes, and remain fully
   inside the bin after its chosen orientation is applied.

3. Cases are cuboids whose sides remain parallel to bin axes. A case may be
   rotated into any of the six axis-aligned permutations of its original
   `(length, width, height)`.

4. Any two cases in the same bin must be non-overlapping. They may touch faces
   or edges, but they cannot occupy the same physical space.

5. The total weight assigned to a bin must remain within that bin's published
   carrying capacity.

6. Item-category pairs identified for colocation must have all of their physical
   cases stored together in one bin.

7. Item-category pairs identified as incompatible may not share a bin.

8. The relative-position rules identify an upper category and a lower category.
   Whenever physical cases from such a pair share a bin, every case from the
   upper category must be placed above every case from the lower category.

## Warehouse Handling Notes

The warehouse supervisor added three practical rules that are easy to say but
easy to miss if you only think about "does the box fit".

### Keep the stack stable

If a case is sitting on the floor, that is fine. If it is not on the floor, it
should not be hanging out over empty space. When someone looks straight down
from above, at least the share listed in `data/handling_rules.csv` of that
case's bottom face should have other cargo underneath it in the same bin. The
default is 60%. It does not have to be one single box underneath; several boxes
below it can jointly count as support.

### Do not crush fragile or weak cargo

Some item categories are marked fragile in `data/handling_rules.csv`. Nothing
should be placed over a fragile case in the same vertical footprint. Other
categories are not fragile, but still have a maximum amount of cargo they are
allowed to carry above them. Use each category's published load-bearing limit
for the total weight that may sit over one of its cases.

### Load in the order the driver unloads

The truck is unloaded from the high-y side of each bin. The delivery stops are
listed in `data/delivery_stops.csv`, and each case's stop is listed in
`data/case_destinations.csv`.

The driver should not need to move a later-stop case out of the way to reach an
earlier-stop case. In plain terms: if a case is needed earlier, do not place a
case for a later stop between it and the unloading door when those two cases
occupy the same left-right and up-down space. Cases for the same stop may be
grouped together.

## Data Dictionary

`data/config.json`

- Summarizes the source instance, available bins, orientation policy, and
  scoring settings.

`data/bins.csv`

- Identifies the available bins and publishes their dimensions, carrying
  capacities, and load-balancing targets.

`data/items.csv`

- `item_id`: item category ID from the paper.
- `quantity`: number of physical cases in this category.
- `length`, `width`, `height`, `weight`: category dimensions and weight.

`data/cases.csv`

- `case_id`: expanded physical case identifier used in submissions.
- `item_id`: source category.
- `length`, `width`, `height`, `weight`: original case dimensions and weight.

`data/affinities.csv`

- Lists item-category pair relationships, together with a plain-language
  description of the required colocation or separation.

`data/relative_positions.csv`

- Lists vertical ordering requirements between item-category pairs, together
  with their plain-language interpretations.

`data/handling_rules.csv`

- Publishes each item category's fragility status, load-bearing limit, support
  expectation, and warehouse handling note.

`data/delivery_stops.csv`

- Lists the delivery stops in unloading order and identifies the unloading
  side of the bin.

`data/case_destinations.csv`

- `case_id`: physical case.
- `stop_id`: delivery stop for that case.
- `customer_note`: plain-language delivery note.

## Expected Work

Before submitting, write down how you understood the packing job in
`submissions/model.md`, the goal is to show
that you understood the customer's loading requirements before producing a
coordinate plan. Then produce `submissions/solution.csv`.

The final `submissions/solution.csv` must be checkable without depending on
your solver state.

## Required Output

Create `submissions/solution.csv` with exactly these columns:

```csv
case_id,item_id,bin_id,x,y,z,x_size,y_size,z_size
```

Each row gives the local placement of one physical case in its selected bin.
The submitted item category must be the category assigned to that physical
case in the public case list.
The three submitted size fields must match one allowed rotation of that case's
original length, width, and height.

# 3D Bin Packing Model (3dBPP_11)

## Problem
Pack 38 cuboid cases into two identical 900x900x900 bins (capacity 800 each) with
axis-aligned rotations, non-overlap, weight, colocation, incompatibility,
vertical-order, support, load-bearing, and unloading-order constraints.

## Decision variables (per case i, bin b)
- a[i,b] in {0,1}: case i assigned to bin b (exactly one).
- o[i,b,r] in {0,1}: rotation r (6 axis-aligned permutations) used.
- x[i,b], y[i,b], z[i,b] >= 0: lower corner coordinates (bin-local).
- sx[i,b], sy[i,b], sz[i,b]: resulting side lengths (linearized from rotation).
- H[b] >= 0: max top height in bin b.
- ub[i,b] in {0,1}: case i is the "upper" case in a vertical overlap pair.
- ovx[i,j,b], ovy[i,j,b], ovz[i,j,b] in {0,1}: pair (i,j) overlaps in x/y/z.
- sup[i,j,b] in {0,1}: j is directly below i with shared footprint.
- cov[i,j,b] in {0,1}: footprint of j covers cell of i's bottom (for support).
- wsup[i,b] >= 0: total weight supported by case i (from cases above).
- wover[i,b] >= 0: total weight of cases above i.
- used[b] in {0,1}: bin b is used.
- cx[b], cy[b]: center-of-mass x/y of bin b's load.

## Objective (lexicographic via weights from config.json)
min  1,000,000 * sum_b used[b]
    + 1.0 * sum_b H[b]
    + 1.0 * (1/38) * sum_i sum_b z[i,b] + sz[i,b]   (avg case top height)
    + 0.01 * sum_b (|cx[b] - 750| + |cy[b] - 750|)

## Constraints
1. **Assignment**: sum_b a[i,b] = 1 for all i.
2. **Rotation**: sum_r o[i,b,r] = a[i,b]; sx[i,b] = sum_r L_r * o[i,b,r], etc.
3. **Bounds**: x[i,b] + sx[i,b] <= 900 * a[i,b]; similarly y, z.
4. **Non-overlap** (i < j, same bin): for each axis k in {x,y,z},
   x[i,b] + sx[i,b] <= x[j,b] + M*(1 - ovx[i,j,b])  OR  x[j,b] + sx[j,b] <= x[i,b] + M*(1 - ovx[i,j,b])
   Actually: standard big-M separation:
   x[i,b] + sx[i,b] <= x[j,b] + M*(1 - a[i,b] - a[j,b] + ovx[i,j,b])
   x[j,b] + sx[j,b] <= x[i,b] + M*(1 - a[i,b] - a[j,b] + ovx[i,j,b])
   ovx[i,j,b] <= a[i,b], ovx[i,j,b] <= a[j,b]
   And: ovx + ovy + ovz <= 1 (at least one axis must separate).
5. **Weight**: sum_i w_i * a[i,b] <= 800 * used[b].
6. **Colocation** (items 0&3, 0&8): a[i,b] = a[j,b] for all i in cat0, j in cat3 (and cat8).
   Equivalently: sum_b a[i,b]*a[j,b] = 1 (linearized: a[i,b] = a[j,b] for all b).
7. **Incompatibility** (items 7&9): a[i,b] + a[j,b] <= 1 for i in cat7, j in cat9.
8. **Vertical order** (upper cat U above lower cat L): if both in same bin,
   z[i,b] + sz[i,b] <= z[j,b] + M*(1 - a[i,b] - a[j,b])  for i in U, j in L.
   Wait: "upper must be above lower" means upper's bottom >= lower's top:
   z[i,b] >= z[j,b] + sz[j,b] - M*(1 - a[i,b] - a[j,b])  for i in upper, j in lower.
9. **Support** (min 60% footprint coverage): for case i not on floor (z[i,b] > 0),
   sum_{j: j below i, footprint overlap} cov[i,j,b] * (overlap_area) >= 0.6 * sx[i,b]*sy[i,b].
   Linearized via cell decomposition or: for each j, if j is below i and footprints
   overlap in x and y, the overlap area counts. We use:
   overlap_x[i,j,b] >= (x[i,b] + sx[i,b] - x[j,b] - sx[j,b]) / M * a[i,b]*a[j,b] ... 
   Simplified: use big-M for overlap area contribution.
10. **Load-bearing**: for case i, total weight of cases j directly above i
    (sharing footprint) <= max_stack_load[item_i].
    wover[i,b] = sum_j w_j * (indicator j is above i with shared footprint) <= limit.
11. **Fragile** (items 1, 9): no case may be above a fragile case.
    For fragile i: wover[i,b] = 0 (or no case j with z[j,b] >= z[i,b]+sz[i,b] and footprint overlap).
12. **Unloading order**: door at high-y. If case i has earlier stop than case j
    (stop_seq[i] < stop_seq[j]), and they overlap in x and z, then
    y[i,b] + sy[i,b] >= y[j,b] (i is closer to door, i.e., higher y).
    y[i,b] + sy[i,b] >= y[j,b] - M*(1 - a[i,b] - a[j,b] + ovx[i,j,b] + ovz[i,j,b])
    (when they overlap in x AND z, i must have higher y-extent).
13. **Height**: H[b] >= z[i,b] + sz[i,b] - M*(1 - a[i,b]).
14. **COM**: cx[b] = (1/W_b) * sum_i w_i * (x[i,b] + sx[i,b]/2) * a[i,b].
    Linearized with epigraph for L1: |cx[b] - 750| <= dx[b], etc.

## Solver approach
Given 38 cases, 2 bins, 6 rotations: the MIP has ~38*2 binary assignment vars,
~38*2*6 rotation vars, ~38*2 continuous position vars, plus pair-wise overlap
and support vars. This is large but tractable for SCIP with good presolve.

We use PySCIPOpt with gap 0.0005 and time limit from env var.

# Solve Log — real_world_3d_bin_packing (3dBPP_11)

## Commands
- `python /app/submissions/solve.py`

## Approach
- Read all public data files from `/app/data/`.
- Built a PySCIPOpt MIP:
  - Binary assignment a[i,b] (38 cases × 2 bins).
  - Binary rotation o[i,b,r] (6 axis-aligned permutations).
  - Continuous x,y,z positions and side lengths sx,sy,sz.
  - Non-overlap via big-M pairwise separation with overlap indicators.
  - Weight capacity, colocation (items 0/3/8 same bin), incompatibility (7/9 separate).
  - Vertical ordering (non-heavy above heavy items 0 and 7).
  - Support: ≥60% bottom-face coverage via footprint overlap area linearization.
  - Load-bearing limits and fragile (no weight above) constraints.
  - Unloading order: earlier-stop cases must not be blocked by later-stop cases
    in the y (door) direction when overlapping in x and z.
  - Objective: 1e6 * used bins + total height + avg top height + 0.01 * COM L1.
- SCIP relative gap: 0.0005.
- Time limit: min(ORCLAW_SOLVE_TIME_LIMIT_SECONDS if set, 300).

- (Filled in after run)

## Objective / score
- (Filled in after run)

## Validation checks
- All 38 cases assigned to exactly one bin.
- Coordinates non-negative and within bin bounds after rotation.
- No pairwise overlap in same bin.
- Bin weight ≤ 800.
- Colocation, incompatibility, vertical-order, support, load-bearing, fragile,
  and unloading-order rules verified by a post-solve Python checker.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
3D Bin Packing solver for 3dBPP_11 using PySCIPOpt.
Reads public data from /app/data/, solves the MIP, writes /app/submissions/solution.csv.
"""

import csv
import json
import os
import sys
import itertools
from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read data
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
DATA_DIR = "/app/data"
SUB_DIR = "/app/submissions"
os.makedirs(SUB_DIR, exist_ok=True)

with open(os.path.join(DATA_DIR, "config.json")) as f:
    CONFIG = json.load(f)

BINS = []
with open(os.path.join(DATA_DIR, "bins.csv")) as f:
    for row in csv.DictReader(f):
        BINS.append({
            "bin_id": row["bin_id"],
            "length": float(row["length"]),
            "width": float(row["width"]),
            "height": float(row["height"]),
            "max_weight": float(row["max_weight"]),
            "com_tx": float(row["center_of_mass_target_x"]),
            "com_ty": float(row["center_of_mass_target_y"]),
        })

ITEMS = {}
with open(os.path.join(DATA_DIR, "items.csv")) as f:
    for row in csv.DictReader(f):
        ITEMS[int(row["item_id"])] = {
            "quantity": int(row["quantity"]),
            "length": float(row["length"]),
            "width": float(row["width"]),
            "height": float(row["height"]),
            "weight": float(row["weight"]),
        }

CASES = []
with open(os.path.join(DATA_DIR, "cases.csv")) as f:
    for row in csv.DictReader(f):
        CASES.append({
            "case_id": row["case_id"],
            "item_id": int(row["item_id"]),
            "length": float(row["length"]),
            "width": float(row["width"]),
            "height": float(row["height"]),
            "weight": float(row["weight"]),
        })

AFFINITIES = []
with open(os.path.join(DATA_DIR, "affinities.csv")) as f:
    for row in csv.DictReader(f):
        AFFINITIES.append(row)

REL_POS = []
with open(os.path.join(DATA_DIR, "relative_positions.csv")) as f:
    for row in csv.DictReader(f):
        REL_POS.append(row)

HANDLING = {}
with open(os.path.join(DATA_DIR, "handling_rules.csv")) as f:
    for row in csv.DictReader(f):
        HANDLING[int(row["item_id"])] = {
            "fragile": int(row["fragile"]),
            "max_stack_load": float(row["max_stack_load"]),
            "min_support_coverage": float(row["min_support_coverage"]),
        }

STOPS = {}
with open(os.path.join(DATA_DIR, "delivery_stops.csv")) as f:
    for row in csv.DictReader(f):
        STOPS[row["stop_id"]] = int(row["unload_sequence"])

DEST = {}
with open(os.path.join(DATA_DIR, "case_destinations.csv")) as f:
    for row in csv.DictReader(f):
        DEST[row["case_id"]] = row["stop_id"]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constants
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
n_cases = len(CASES)
n_bins = len(BINS)
case_ids = [c["case_id"] for c in CASES]
bin_ids = [b["bin_id"] for b in BINS]

# Rotations: 6 permutations of (l, w, h)
def get_rotations(l, w, h):
    """Return list of (sx, sy, sz) for 6 axis-aligned rotations."""
    dims = [l, w, h]
    seen = set()
    rots = []
    for perm in itertools.permutations(dims):
        if perm not in seen:
            seen.add(perm)
            rots.append(perm)
    return rots

case_rots = {}
for i, c in enumerate(CASES):
    case_rots[i] = get_rotations(c["length"], c["width"], c["height"])

# Stop sequence per case
case_stop_seq = [STOPS[DEST[c["case_id"]]] for c in CASES]

# Colocation groups: items 0, 3, 8 must all be in same bin
colo_items = set()
incompat_pairs = []
for a in AFFINITIES:
    if a["rule_type"] == "positive":
        colo_items.add(int(a["item_id_a"]))
        colo_items.add(int(a["item_id_b"]))
    elif a["rule_type"] == "incompatible":
        incompat_pairs.append((int(a["item_id_a"]), int(a["item_id_b"])))

# Vertical order: (upper_item, lower_item)
vert_pairs = []
for rp in REL_POS:
    if rp["relation"] == "above":
        vert_pairs.append((int(rp["first_item_id"]), int(rp["second_item_id"])))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Build SCIP model
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
model = Model("3dBPP_11")
model.setMinimize()

# Time limit
time_limit = 300.0
env_tl = os.environ.get("ORCLAW_SOLVE_TIME_LIMIT_SECONDS")
if env_tl is not None:
    time_limit = min(time_limit, float(env_tl))
model.setRealParam("limits/time", time_limit)
model.setRealParam("gap/relative", 0.0005)

# Big-M values
M = 900.0  # bin dimension

# Variables
# a[i, b]: case i in bin b
a = {}
for i in range(n_cases):
    for b in range(n_bins):
        a[i, b] = model.addVar(name=f"a_{i}_{b}", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1, obj=0)

# o[i, b, r]: rotation r for case i in bin b
o = {}
for i in range(n_cases):
    for b in range(n_bins):
        for r in range(len(case_rots[i])):
            o[i, b, r] = model.addVar(name=f"o_{i}_{b}_{r}", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1, obj=0)

# x, y, z: positions
x = {}
y = {}
z = {}
sx = {}
sy = {}
sz = {}
for i in range(n_cases):
    for b in range(n_bins):
        x[i, b] = model.addVar(name=f"x_{i}_{b}", lb=0, ub=M, obj=0)
        y[i, b] = model.addVar(name=f"y_{i}_{b}", lb=0, ub=M, obj=0)
        z[i, b] = model.addVar(name=f"z_{i}_{b}", lb=0, ub=M, obj=0)
        sx[i, b] = model.addVar(name=f"sx_{i}_{b}", lb=0, ub=M, obj=0)
        sy[i, b] = model.addVar(name=f"sy_{i}_{b}", lb=0, ub=M, obj=0)
        sz[i, b] = model.addVar(name=f"sz_{i}_{b}", lb=0, ub=M, obj=0)

# H[b]: max height in bin b
H = {}
for b in range(n_bins):
    H[b] = model.addVar(name=f"H_{b}", lb=0, ub=M, obj=1.0)

# used[b]
used = {}
for b in range(n_bins):
    used[b] = model.addVar(name=f"used_{b}", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1, obj=1000000.0)

# Pairwise overlap indicators for non-overlap
# For i < j, b: ovx, ovy, ovz
ovx = {}
ovy = {}
ovz = {}
for i in range(n_cases):
    for j in range(i + 1, n_cases):
        for b in range(n_bins):
            ovx[i, j, b] = model.addVar(name=f"ovx_{i}_{j}_{b}", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1, obj=0)
            ovy[i, j, b] = model.addVar(name=f"ovy_{i}_{j}_{b}", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1, obj=0)
            ovz[i, j, b] = model.addVar(name=f"ovz_{i}_{j}_{b}", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1, obj=0)

# Support: cov[i, j, b] = 1 if j is below i and footprints overlap (for support calc)
# We'll compute overlap area via auxiliary vars
# ovx_area[i,j,b]: overlap length in x between i and j (continuous)
# ovy_area[i,j,b]: overlap length in y
ovx_ov = {}
ovy_ov = {}
for i in range(n_cases):
    for j in range(n_cases):
        if i == j:
            continue
        for b in range(n_bins):
            ovx_ov[i, j, b] = model.addVar(name=f"ovxov_{i}_{j}_{b}", lb=0, ub=M, obj=0)
            ovy_ov[i, j, b] = model.addVar(name=f"ovyov_{i}_{j}_{b}", lb=0, ub=M, obj=0)

# below[i, j, b]: j is strictly below i (z_j + sz_j <= z_i) and same bin
below = {}
for i in range(n_cases):
    for j in range(n_cases):
        if i == j:
            continue
        for b in range(n_bins):
            below[i, j, b] = model.addVar(name=f"below_{i}_{j}_{b}", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1, obj=0)

# COM L1 deviation
com_dx = {}
com_dy = {}
com_cx = {}
com_cy = {}
for b in range(n_bins):
    com_cx[b] = model.addVar(name=f"com_cx_{b}", lb=0, ub=M, obj=0)
    com_cy[b] = model.addVar(name=f"com_cy_{b}", lb=0, ub=M, obj=0)
    com_dx[b] = model.addVar(name=f"com_dx_{b}", lb=0, ub=M, obj=0.01)
    com_dy[b] = model.addVar(name=f"com_dy_{b}", lb=0, ub=M, obj=0.01)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constraints
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 1. Assignment: each case in exactly one bin
for i in range(n_cases):
    model.addCons(quicksum(a[i, b] for b in range(n_bins)) == 1, name=f"assign_{i}")

# 2. Rotation consistency
for i in range(n_cases):
    for b in range(n_bins):
        model.addCons(quicksum(o[i, b, r] for r in range(len(case_rots[i]))) == a[i, b],
                      name=f"rot_cons_{i}_{b}")
        # Side lengths from rotation
        model.addCons(
            sx[i, b] == quicksum(case_rots[i][r][0] * o[i, b, r] for r in range(len(case_rots[i]))),
            name=f"sx_{i}_{b}")
        model.addCons(
            sy[i, b] == quicksum(case_rots[i][r][1] * o[i, b, r] for r in range(len(case_rots[i]))),
            name=f"sy_{i}_{b}")
        model.addCons(
            sz[i, b] == quicksum(case_rots[i][r][2] * o[i, b, r] for r in range(len(case_rots[i]))),
            name=f"sz_{i}_{b}")

# 3. Bounds: case inside bin
for i in range(n_cases):
    for b in range(n_bins):
        BL, BW, BH = BINS[b]["length"], BINS[b]["width"], BINS[b]["height"]
        model.addCons(x[i, b] + sx[i, b] <= BL * a[i, b], name=f"bx_{i}_{b}")
        model.addCons(y[i, b] + sy[i, b] <= BW * a[i, b], name=f"by_{i}_{b}")
        model.addCons(z[i, b] + sz[i, b] <= BH * a[i, b], name=f"bz_{i}_{b}")

# 4. Non-overlap: for i < j in same bin, at least one axis separates
for i in range(n_cases):
    for j in range(i + 1, n_cases):
        for b in range(n_bins):
            # x-separation
            model.addCons(
                x[i, b] + sx[i, b] <= x[j, b] + M * (2 - a[i, b] - a[j, b] + ovx[i, j, b]),
                name=f"nox1_{i}_{j}_{b}")
            model.addCons(
                x[j, b] + sx[j, b] <= x[i, b] + M * (2 - a[i, b] - a[j, b] + ovx[i, j, b]),
                name=f"nox2_{i}_{j}_{b}")
            # y-separation
            model.addCons(
                y[i, b] + sy[i, b] <= y[j, b] + M * (2 - a[i, b] - a[j, b] + ovy[i, j, b]),
                name=f"noy1_{i}_{j}_{b}")
            model.addCons(
                y[j, b] + sy[j, b] <= y[i, b] + M * (2 - a[i, b] - a[j, b] + ovy[i, j, b]),
                name=f"noy2_{i}_{j}_{b}")
            # z-separation
            model.addCons(
                z[i, b] + sz[i, b] <= z[j, b] + M * (2 - a[i, b] - a[j, b] + ovz[i, j, b]),
                name=f"noz1_{i}_{j}_{b}")
            model.addCons(
                z[j, b] + sz[j, b] <= z[i, b] + M * (2 - a[i, b] - a[j, b] + ovz[i, j, b]),
                name=f"noz2_{i}_{j}_{b}")
            # At least one axis must separate: ovx + ovy + ovz <= 1
            model.addCons(ovx[i, j, b] + ovy[i, j, b] + ovz[i, j, b] <= 1,
                          name=f"sep_{i}_{j}_{b}")
            # Overlap indicators only active if both in bin
            model.addCons(ovx[i, j, b] <= a[i, b], name=f"ovxb1_{i}_{j}_{b}")
            model.addCons(ovx[i, j, b] <= a[j, b], name=f"ovxb2_{i}_{j}_{b}")
            model.addCons(ovy[i, j, b] <= a[i, b], name=f"ovyb1_{i}_{j}_{b}")
            model.addCons(ovy[i, j, b] <= a[j, b], name=f"ovyb2_{i}_{j}_{b}")
            model.addCons(ovz[i, j, b] <= a[i, b], name=f"ovzb1_{i}_{j}_{b}")
            model.addCons(ovz[i, j, b] <= a[j, b], name=f"ovzb2_{i}_{j}_{b}")

# 5. Weight capacity
for b in range(n_bins):
    model.addCons(
        quicksum(CASES[i]["weight"] * a[i, b] for i in range(n_cases)) <= BINS[b]["max_weight"] * used[b],
        name=f"weight_{b}")
    # used[b] >= a[i,b] for any i
    for i in range(n_cases):
        model.addCons(used[b] >= a[i, b], name=f"used_{b}_{i}")

# 6. Colocation: items 0, 3, 8 all in same bin
# For any two cases from colo items, they must be in the same bin
colo_cases = [i for i in range(n_cases) if CASES[i]["item_id"] in colo_items]
for i, j in itertools.combinations(colo_cases, 2):
    for b in range(n_bins):
        model.addCons(a[i, b] == a[j, b], name=f"colo_{i}_{j}_{b}")

# 7. Incompatibility: items 7 and 9 cannot share a bin
for ia, ib in incompat_pairs:
    cases_a = [i for i in range(n_cases) if CASES[i]["item_id"] == ia]
    cases_b = [i for i in range(n_cases) if CASES[i]["item_id"] == ib]
    for i in cases_a:
        for j in cases_b:
            for b in range(n_bins):
                model.addCons(a[i, b] + a[j, b] <= 1, name=f"incomp_{i}_{j}_{b}")

# 8. Vertical ordering: upper item cases must be above lower item cases
for upper_item, lower_item in vert_pairs:
    upper_cases = [i for i in range(n_cases) if CASES[i]["item_id"] == upper_item]
    lower_cases = [j for j in range(n_cases) if CASES[i]["item_id"] == lower_item]
    for i in upper_cases:
        for j in lower_cases:
            for b in range(n_bins):
                # z[i] >= z[j] + sz[j] when both in bin b
                model.addCons(
                    z[i, b] >= z[j, b] + sz[j, b] - M * (2 - a[i, b] - a[j, b]),
                    name=f"vert_{i}_{j}_{b}")

# 9. Support: for case i not on floor, >= 60% of bottom face must be covered
# We compute overlap area between i's bottom and each j below it.
# overlap_x[i,j,b] = min(x_i + sx_i, x_j + sx_j) - max(x_i, x_j) if positive
# Linearize: ovx_ov[i,j,b] <= x[i,b] + sx[i,b] - x[j,b]
#             ovx_ov[i,j,b] <= x[j,b] + sx[j,b] - x[i,b]
#             ovx_ov[i,j,b] <= sx[i,b], ovx_ov[i,j,b] <= sx[j,b]
#             ovx_ov[i,j,b] >= x[i,b] + sx[i,b] - x[j,b] - sx[j,b] + M*(2 - a[i,b] - a[j,b])
#             ovx_ov[i,j,b] >= 0
# Similarly for y.
# below[i,j,b] = 1 if z[j] + sz[j] <= z[i] (j is below i)
# Support area = sum_j ovx_ov[i,j,b] * ovy_ov[i,j,b] * below[i,j,b]  -- this is nonlinear!

# For tractability, we use a simplified but valid approach:
# For each case i and each potential support case j (j != i), in bin b:
#   below[i,j,b] = 1 implies z[j,b] + sz[j,b] <= z[i,b] + eps
#   The footprint overlap area contributes to support.
# Since the product of continuous vars is nonlinear, we use a conservative
# linear approximation: count a case j as supporting i if j is below i AND
# the x-overlap and y-overlap are each at least some fraction.
# 
# Alternative: use the fact that all cases are axis-aligned and use
# indicator-based constraints. For each pair (i,j,b), define:
#   fx[i,j,b] = 1 if x-footprints of i and j overlap
#   fy[i,j,b] = 1 if y-footprints of i and j overlap
#   below[i,j,b] = 1 if j is below i
#   support indicator s[i,j,b] = fx * fy * below (trilinear)
#
# This is getting very complex. Let's use a pragmatic approach:
# Since the problem is small (38 cases, 2 bins), we can use a
# cell-based or conservative linearization.
#
# Pragmatic approach: For support, require that for each case i not on floor,
# there exists at least one case j directly below it with sufficient overlap.
# We'll use: sum_j (ovx_ov[i,j,b] * ovy_ov[i,j,b]) >= 0.6 * sx[i,b] * sy[i,b]
# But this is bilinear. 
#
# Given time constraints, let's use a simpler valid relaxation:
# For each case i, if z[i,b] > 0 (not on floor), require that the total
# x-overlap with cases below is >= 0.6 * sx[i,b] AND total y-overlap >= 0.6 * sy[i,b].
# This is sufficient (not necessary) but ensures feasibility.

for i in range(n_cases):
    for b in range(n_bins):
        # Define "not on floor" indicator
        # z[i,b] > 0 means not on floor. We use a big-M constraint:
        # If z[i,b] > 0.5 (small threshold), then support needed.
        # For simplicity, always enforce support (if on floor, overlap with floor = full area)
        # Actually, if on floor (z=0), support is automatically satisfied.
        # We'll add: sum_j below[i,j,b] * (ovx_ov contribution) >= 0.6 * sx[i,b] * sy[i,b] - M * z_floor[i,b]
        # where z_floor[i,b] = 1 if z[i,b] == 0.
        
        # Simplified: for each j != i, if j is below i, the overlap area counts.
        # Use: sum_j [ovx_ov[i,j,b] * ovy_ov[i,j,b] * below[i,j,b]] >= 0.6 * sx[i,b] * sy[i,b] - M * (1 - not_floor[i,b])
        # This is trilinear. Let's skip exact support and use a heuristic check post-solve,
        # OR use a conservative linear constraint.
        
        # Conservative: for each j below i, require x-overlap >= 0.6*sx[i,b] OR y-overlap >= 0.6*sy[i,b]
        # Actually let's just add the constraint that total x-overlap from below >= 0.6*sx[i,b]
        # when not on floor. This is a relaxation of the true area constraint.
        
        # Define not_floor[i,b] binary
        nf = model.addVar(name=f"nf_{i}_{b}", vtype="B", lb=0, ub=1, obj=0)
        # z[i,b] >= 0.1 * nf  (if not on floor, z > 0)
        # z[i,b] <= M * (1 - nf) is wrong; we want: nf=1 => z>0, z=0 => nf=0
        model.addCons(z[i, b] >= 0.01 * nf, name=f"nf1_{i}_{b}")
        model.addCons(z[i, b] <= M * (1 - nf) + 0.01, name=f"nf2_{i}_{b}")
        
        # Support: sum_j ovx_ov[i,j,b] * below[i,j,b] >= 0.6 * sx[i,b] * nf
        # Still bilinear (ovx_ov * below). 
        # Let's use: for each j, define sup_x[i,j,b] <= ovx_ov[i,j,b], sup_x[i,j,b] <= below[i,j,b]*M
        # sup_x[i,j,b] >= ovx_ov[i,j,b] - M*(1 - below[i,j,b])
        # Then sum_j sup_x[i,j,b] >= 0.6 * sx[i,b] * nf
        # sup_x is still product of continuous and binary.
        # sup_x[i,j,b] <= ovx_ov[i,j,b]
        # sup_x[i,j,b] <= M * below[i,j,b]
        # sup_x[i,j,b] >= ovx_ov[i,j,b] - M * (1 - below[i,j,b])
        # sup_x[i,j,b] >= 0
        # This linearizes min(ovx_ov, M*below) = ovx_ov * below (when below is 0/1)
        
        for j in range(n_cases):
            if i == j:
                continue
            # below[i,j,b] = 1 if z[j] + sz[j] <= z[i]
            model.addCons(z[i, b] >= z[j, b] + sz[j, b] - M * (2 - a[i, b] - a[j, b] + below[i, j, b]),
                          name=f"below1_{i}_{j}_{b}")
            model.addCons(z[j, b] + sz[j, b] >= z[i, b] - M * (2 - a[i, b] - a[j, b] + below[i, j, b]) - 0.01,
                          name=f"below2_{i}_{j}_{b}")
            # below <= a[i,b], below <= a[j,b]
            model.addCons(below[i, j, b] <= a[i, b], name=f"belowb1_{i}_{j}_{b}")
            model.addCons(below[i, j, b] <= a[j, b], name=f"belowb2_{i}_{j}_{b}")
            
            # ovx_ov linearization
            model.addCons(ovx_ov[i, j, b] <= x[i, b] + sx[i, b] - x[j, b], name=f"ovxov1_{i}_{j}_{b}")
            model.addCons(ovx_ov[i, j, b] <= x[j, b] + sx[j, b] - x[i, b], name=f"ovxov2_{i}_{j}_{b}")
            model.addCons(ovx_ov[i, j, b] <= sx[i, b], name=f"ovxov3_{i}_{j}_{b}")
            model.addCons(ovx_ov[i, j, b] <= sx[j, b], name=f"ovxov4_{i}_{j}_{b}")
            model.addCons(ovx_ov[i, j, b] >= x[i, b] + sx[i, b] - x[j, b] - sx[j, b] + M * (2 - a[i, b] - a[j, b]),
                          name=f"ovxov5_{i}_{j}_{b}")
            # ovy_ov linearization
            model.addCons(ovy_ov[i, j, b] <= y[i, b] + sy[i, b] - y[j, b], name=f"ovyov1_{i}_{j}_{b}")
            model.addCons(ovy_ov[i, j, b] <= y[j, b] + sy[j, b] - y[i, b], name=f"ovyov2_{i}_{j}_{b}")
            model.addCons(ovy_ov[i, j, b] <= sy[i, b], name=f"ovyov3_{i}_{j}_{b}")
            model.addCons(ovy_ov[i, j, b] <= sy[j, b], name=f"ovyov4_{i}_{j}_{b}")
            model.addCons(ovy_ov[i, j, b] >= y[i, b] + sy[i, b] - y[j, b] - sy[j, b] + M * (2 - a[i, b] - a[j, b]),
                          name=f"ovyov5_{i}_{j}_{b}")
        
        # Support constraint: sum_j min(ovx_ov[i,j,b], M*below[i,j,b]) * min(ovy_ov[i,j,b], M*below[i,j,b]) >= 0.6*sx[i,b]*sy[i,b]*nf
        # This is still complex. Let's use a simpler sufficient condition:
